messages:
Maya (Support): incoming escalation from a couple of customers — p99 latency spiking on hosted route /v1/chat/completions in us-east, started ~2026-03-15T03:10Z. multiple users reporting timeouts and retries. attaching metrics screenshot: <link>
redwood-monitor-bot: Alert: route_latency_p99 > 1500ms for 5m on route=chat-v1-us-east (alert_id: A-4883)
Maya (Support): root cause unknown, creating thread here. customers say successes drop and retries pile up.
Ravi (oncall-sre): on it. which model + any recent deploys?
Maya (Support): model: rwd-llama-1.1-instruct-16k (hosted), recent config change? Customer says they sent larger batched prompts around the spike.
Lina (eng-runtime): checking dashboards now. quick PromQL to eyeball queueing:
```
sum by (worker) (rate(redwood_inference_queue_length[5m]))
sum by (route) (increases(redwood_admission_control_rejected_total[5m]))
```
Lina (eng-runtime): I'm seeing queue_length jump 20x at 03:10 and admission_control_rejected spiking — concurrent inflight tokens > concurrency_limit, so requests are being queued and then sometimes rejected. p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~600ms, p99 peaked ~2.1s.
Arjun (Infra): GPU metrics show worker pods at ~98% GPU util and steady 95% memory. Horizontal autoscaler didn't add nodes — autoscaler threshold not hit bc scheduler thinks pods are fine, but per-pod concurrency limit is bottleneck. looks like a config roll that reduced per-worker concurrency for this model last week (maybe rollout 2026-03-08?)
Ravi (oncall-sre): ok immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily increase per-route concurrency limit; 2) enable burst capacity; 3) put heavy customers on fallback smaller model if needed. Lina, can we increase concurrency safely for this route?
Lina (eng-runtime): yes we can bump but watch GPU OOM. propose conservative bump 16 -> 24 and burst=8. command:
```
# local redwoodctl (config change, no deploy)
redwoodctl route update --route chat-v1-us-east --model rwd-llama-1.1-instruct-16k --concurrency-limit 24 --burst 8
```
Ravi (oncall-sre): applying now.
deploy-bot: config-change: route chat-v1-us-east concurrency-limit updated 16->24 by @Ravi (change_id c-8931)
redwood-monitor-bot: Scaling decision: burst mode enabled for route chat-v1-us-east
Maya (Support): told customers we're applying mitigation and will follow up. asked them to throttle retry loops for 10m.
Lina (eng-runtime): after ~2m post-change, queue_length back down ~80%, p95 ~170ms, p99 ~720ms — improved but not fully to baseline. still seeing short spikes when large batch requests arrive.
Arjun (Infra): next quick mitigation: enable automated fallback routing for top noisy API keys — route heavy keys to rwd-llama-1.1-quantized or rwd-llama-1.0-small. sample policy:
```
route.policy.fallback = {
  "match": "api_key in [\"kabc123\", \"kxyz789\"]",
  "fallback_model": "rwd-llama-1.1-int8",
  "reason": "reduce per-request GPU time during backpressure"
}
```
Harper (Product): agree. notify affected customers we're routing them to lower-latency quantized model as a temporary measure and offering credits. Maya can you draft a short note? keep it simple: we mitigated, working on root cause, will follow-up.
Maya (Support): drafting msg: "We've enabled temporary routing to a lower-latency variant and increased concurrency to reduce queuing. Recommend adding exponential backoff on retries. We'll share a postmortem." will send.
Lina (eng-runtime): log snippet from admission controller during spike:
```
2026-03-15T03:11:05Z admission_controller.go:214 WARN reject request token=abcd reason=concurrency_limit_reached route=chat-v1-us-east
2026-03-15T03:11:06Z queue_manager.go:89 INFO enqueued request id=... queue_len=42
```
Ravi (oncall-sre): created incident INC-2026-742 and assigned to eng-runtime + infra. short-term owner = @Lina, infra follow-up = @Arjun. ticket link: <internal/INC-2026-742>
Arjun (Infra): adding autoscaler tweak: lower GPU_utilization_target from 85->75 and allow faster scale-up. will roll in 10m if no objections.
Lina (eng-runtime): agree. also adding synthetic load test to run at 03:00 daily to catch regressions in concurrency behavior.
Harper (Product): add customer-facing note to status page and include mitigations. also track cost impact of increased concurrency/burst.
Ravi (oncall-sre): current status: p95 ~160-200ms, p99 ~600-800ms. marking incident as mitigated for now. will keep thread open for postmortem.
Maya (Support): customers acknowledged the mitigation, one asks for ETA for root cause — telling them we'll have update in 48h.
Lina (eng-runtime): preliminary root cause hypothesis: config rollout last week lowered default per-worker concurrency for certain LLM families to reduce tail CPU spikes; combined with a burst of larger batched prompts and retry storms caused queueing to pile up. follow-ups: revert risky rollout or make it model-family-specific and add canary with synthetic traffic.
Arjun (Infra): follow-ups I own: 1) autoscaler tuning, 2) add pod-level queue_len metric to node exporter, 3) rollout audit to find when concurrency change was applied.
Lina (eng-runtime): follow-ups I own: 1) improve admission_control algorithm to account for batch size distribution, 2) implement automatic fallback policy when admission rejects exceed threshold, 3) add a Grafana alert for queue_len > 10 for >2m.
Ravi (oncall-sre): I'll run a quick post-incident summary and schedule a deeper postmortem meeting. tagging this thread for postmortem notes.
Maya (Support): thanks everyone. will update customers after postmortem. :thumbsup:
